meta.title: Item detail
meta.description: What opens when a reader activates an item, what the default dialog shows, and how to replace it.

basics.intro: Activating an item — a card, a pinned chip, a row in the overflow table — opens its detail. The default is a modal dialog with the level and the title, the description, the pills, the time and a close button. Which item is open is openItemId, controlled or uncontrolled like the rest of the state.
points: Activation runs handlers.onItemActivate first, which can cancel it, then sets the id, then calls onItemOpen.
An item marked disabled does not open.
If the open item disappears from items, the detail closes with the reason itemRemoved and does not reopen by itself.
Closing returns focus to whatever opened it; when that element is gone, focus goes to the scroller.

own.intro: renderItemDetail replaces the dialog entirely — with a drawer, a panel beside the schedule, or a route of its own. It receives the item, how it was opened, and a function that closes it.
own.state: Because openItemId is ordinary state, a detail of your own can also be opened from outside: set the id and the component treats it as an activation, which is how a deep link to one item works.

points: The default detail is a native modal dialog: focus is contained by the browser, <kbd>Escape</kbd> closes it, and the backdrop is a click target.
It is labelled by its title, and its content is read in the order it is drawn.
Focus returns to the activator on close, which is what makes repeated opening and closing bearable with a keyboard.
A detail of your own is yours to make accessible: the component only tells you which item to show and when to close.
renderItemDetail for the whole thing, or the detailDialog part through slots for the dialog itself.
localization.detail.close is the close label of the default dialog.
openItemId, defaultOpenItemId and onOpenItemIdChange hold the state; onItemOpen and onItemClose report it.
The default dialog is in a lazy chunk, loaded the first time an item is opened.
One item is open at a time.
The default dialog shows the fields the item model has; anything else belongs in a detail of your own.
There is no editing in the detail — it shows, it does not change.
